notes: ACCESS: panemirates.com is a marketing redirect to www.panhomestores.com/uae_en/ (Al Seer Group's Pan Home UAE storefront, ScandiPWA on Magento 2, store_code uae_en) - confirmed as the correct live site. Reached ONLY through the Claude-in-Chrome connector in my own tab; no HTTP-layer tooling was used at any point. The origin sits behind a Cloudflare Managed Challenge: the first hit of any URL renders a 'Just a moment...' interstitial which then SELF-CLEARS in real Chrome, so ordinary tab navigation works. BLOCK ENCOUNTERED: the same-origin POST /graphql started returning HTTP 403 after about four successful queries. Per the hard block rule I stopped that route immediately - no retries, no backoff, no waiting - and finished the company through plain page navigation plus DOM reads instead. ROBOTS.TXT: could not be read - the challenge never clears for that non-HTML path. The prior Home-Decor pass recorded 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /', a blanket disallow with NO Claude-specific rule (no ClaudeBot / anthropic-ai / Claude-Web / Claude-User / Claude-SearchBot directive), i.e. an ordinary WAF-protected site rather than a named must-decline case. QTY SOURCE: the site's own RENDERED listing header ('N items') and, for children, the parent listing page's own CATEGORIES layered-nav facet. I verified that the facet equals the child's own rendered header on two independent nodes at two different depths - Sofas facet 884 == sofas page header 884, and Beds facet 245 == beds page header 245 - so facet counts are used as exact per-node totals. MAGENTO product_count IS INFLATED HERE, CONFIRMED, AND WAS NOT USED: categoryList.product_count reported 21694 for Furniture where the rendered header reads 5955 (3.6x), and 1717 for Bedroom where the header reads 1250. Every qty in this file comes from the rendered header or facet, never from product_count. TREE SOURCES (three, cross-checked per trap 1): (a) GraphQL categoryList before it was blocked, which gave the 8 Furniture children; (b) the desktop mega-menu, forced fully open by dispatching mouseenter on every department so all panels rendered, yielding 73 furniture paths; (c) each department page's own CATEGORIES facet. Menu and facet agree exactly on every level-3 node in all 7 departments, and both agree with GraphQL at level 2. The XML sitemap is not usable - the SPA swallows /sitemap.xml and renders an empty 'Menu' route. FACET CAVEAT HANDLED: the CATEGORIES facet can list cross-cut categories that are not path children. 'Kids Accessories (759)' under Kids & Teens and 'Modular (168)' / 'Modulars (155)' under Bedroom / Sofas are such cross-cuts, and I did not treat them as children of those departments. Modular is instead emitted from its own top-level branch modular-furniture, whose three children sum exactly to its header (178+157+88=423). EXCLUDED, with reasons: Mattresses (248, plus Bonnel Spring / Foam / Memory Foam / Pocketed Spring) - bedding, not furniture; Outdoor > Garden Accessories (739) - planters, garden decor and accessories, matching what the prior Home-Decor pass found in that branch; Outdoor > Barbeque and Camping (53); Outdoor > Kids Outdoor Playsets (7) - play equipment; Outdoor > Gazebo and Pergola (13) - garden structures rather than furniture; Living Room > Storage and Organisation (29) - the brief assigns standalone storage and organisers to a future Storage task; Consoles & Mirrors > Mirrors (7) - Wall Decor's job; Kids & Teens > Kids Accessories (759) - cross-cut accessories branch. NOT ROWS (rule 3 landing pages, no listing and no count): /uae_en/department-household and /uae_en/furniture-office are CMS pages whose only links are the main nav - the real office listings are the four furniture/home-office children, which are emitted. 'Online Exclusive upto 80% Off', 'Shop All', 'Package', 'Flat 70/80/90% Off', 'Best Price' and the discount-range entries were dropped as promotional or navigation facets. LIMITATION AFFECTING CLASSIFICATION ONLY, NOT COUNTS: product tiles never hydrate - every card stays a 'ProductCard-VisibilityPlaceholder' with no text, no product anchors and no JSON-LD, because the product-list GraphQL call is exactly the route that is 403'd. I therefore could not run the usual title scan to classify borderline nodes on product evidence, and fell back to the node name plus the site's own placement inside its Furniture department. The nodes where that leaves real doubt carry a MANUAL REVIEW flag; their qty values are still exact site-reported numbers. ALSO UNRESOLVED: furniture/bedroom/bedroom-add-ons returned the SPA's empty 'Menu' route rather than a listing when opened directly (category resolution was degrading by then). Its count of 57 still comes from the parent Bedroom page's own facet, and I did not retry, per the hard block rule. DEPTH DECISIONS: Beds is kept as a leaf because its six children are pure size cuts (King / Queen / Single / Super King / Twin / Day Beds), and Wardrobes likewise (6-Door and Sliding are configuration facets). Dining Chairs and Living Chair each have a single child covering only part of the node (Bench, Accent Chair), so the parent is kept to avoid losing the rest. Consoles & Mirrors is the one case where the child is the right leaf: Consoles (47) is emitted and the 7 mirrors are excluded, leaving 18 console-and-mirror set items on the parent with no dedicated URL. LEAF URLS come from the site's own mega-menu anchors rather than constructed slugs, so trap 2 (a bogus slug silently serving the parent's number) does not apply here; the counts are independently anchored to the parent's facet rather than to whatever a leaf page might render.
